source_opportunity: Supplier invoice and purchase-order PDF line-item extraction

positioning.one_liner: Turn supplier invoice and purchase-order PDFs into reviewable line-item CSV and JSON.
positioning.target_user: Small logistics, manufacturing, trades, procurement and operations teams that re-key supplier documents into spreadsheets.
positioning.painful_job: Manually read supplier invoices and purchase orders, then retype headers and line items such as SKU, quantity, unit price and totals into spreadsheets.
positioning.unique_value: A narrow review-before-export workflow for supplier documents, without claiming perfect extraction or replacing accounting approval.

prd.objective: Reduce repetitive supplier-document re-keying by extracting structured fields from one PDF at a time and requiring human review before export.
prd.user_story: As an operations or admin user, I want to upload a supplier invoice or purchase-order PDF, review and correct the extracted fields, then download CSV or JSON instead of retyping the document.
in_scope: Upload one PDF up to 10 MB
Extract document type, vendor, document number, date, currency and totals
Extract line items including SKU, description, quantity, unit, unit price and line total
Show extracted data in an editable review screen before export
Download reviewed data as CSV or JSON
Validate a Lemon Squeezy subscription license key for paid access
Allow a deliberately limited unlicensed demo only when explicitly enabled by environment configuration
Process documents without adding application-level persistent document storage in the MVP
success_metrics: A user can upload a supported PDF and receive structured fields or a clear recoverable error
A user can correct extracted values before export
CSV and JSON exports reflect the reviewed values
The application never describes AI extraction as guaranteed or error-free
Checkout, license validation and public legal pages pass launch preflight
acceptance_criteria: PDF MIME type and 10 MB maximum are enforced server-side
Missing or uncertain fields may be returned as null rather than invented
The review screen allows editing every extracted header field and line-item field
CSV output contains one row per line item and repeats document-level identifiers
JSON output preserves the complete reviewed document structure
Uploaded PDF bytes are not written to the product database or filesystem by application code
Paid-mode extraction requires a valid license key for the configured Lemon Squeezy variant
Public copy states that users should verify extracted data before relying on it

landing_page.headline: Stop retyping supplier PDFs into spreadsheets.
landing_page.subheadline: Upload a supplier invoice or purchase order, review the extracted header and line items, then export clean CSV or JSON.
problem_bullets: Supplier PDFs arrive in different layouts
Line items such as SKU, quantity and price are tedious to re-key
Manual re-entry creates another place for transcription mistakes
solution_bullets: Extract common supplier-document fields from PDF
Review and correct every extracted value before export
Export reviewed line items to CSV or JSON
landing_page.pricing_anchor: Subscription price is shown on the Pricing page and must match the configured Lemon Squeezy plan.
faq: Does SupplyExtract guarantee every field is correct?
Are uploaded documents stored by the application?

validation_experiments.hypothesis: Small operations teams that currently re-key supplier PDFs will try a focused review-before-export tool.
validation_experiments.audience: Small logistics, manufacturing, trades and procurement teams processing supplier invoices or purchase orders
validation_experiments.channel: Problem-keyword SEO and direct outreach to operations/admin users who describe manual PDF-to-spreadsheet workflows
validation_experiments.offer: Use the live extractor on one real non-sensitive supplier PDF and review the output before exporting
validation_experiments.primary_metric: qualified visitor completes an extraction and reaches the review screen
validation_experiments.pass_threshold: At least 10 qualified users complete a real extraction and at least 3 request continued access or pricing
validation_experiments.fail_threshold: Fewer than 3 qualified users complete a real extraction after targeted outreach to 30 qualified prospects

validation_experiments.hypothesis: Users with recurring document-entry pain will accept a simple monthly subscription rather than a broad enterprise document platform.
validation_experiments.audience: Qualified users who successfully complete the extraction workflow
validation_experiments.channel: In-product pricing page and follow-up with early users
validation_experiments.offer: Monthly access to the current supplier PDF extraction workflow
validation_experiments.primary_metric: qualified users who start or explicitly request the paid subscription
validation_experiments.pass_threshold: At least 3 paid starts or explicit purchase commitments from 15 qualified conversations
validation_experiments.fail_threshold: No paid start or explicit purchase commitment from 15 qualified conversations

pricing_plan: Initial product hypothesis: one monthly subscription for the current supplier PDF extraction workflow. The public price must be sourced from the verified Lemon Squeezy Price object at launch; do not publish a different hard-coded price.

technical_spec.architecture: Next.js App Router web application. Browser uploads a PDF to a server route; the route validates entitlement and file limits, sends the PDF transiently to the configured OpenAI Responses model for structured extraction, returns JSON to an editable client-side review UI, and does not add application-level PDF persistence.
technical_spec.frontend: Next.js + TypeScript client review table with CSV/JSON export
technical_spec.backend: Next.js route handlers using native fetch for OpenAI Responses API and Lemon Squeezy License API
technical_spec.database: No product database required for MVP document processing. Add persistent usage metering before advertising or enforcing a monthly document quota.
integrations: OpenAI Responses API for PDF input and schema-constrained extraction
Lemon Squeezy License API for entitlement validation
Lemon Squeezy signed webhooks for subscription lifecycle
non_functional_requirements: No application-level persistent storage of uploaded PDF bytes
Never log PDF contents or extracted sensitive document fields
Uncertain values should be null or flagged rather than fabricated
OpenAI and Lemon Squeezy secrets remain server-side
Public privacy copy accurately discloses third-party document processing
No unsupported accuracy, customer, security-certification or retention claims

builder_manifest.build_goal: Ship a review-ready supplier invoice / purchase-order PDF extractor that produces editable structured data and CSV/JSON export.

tasks.title: Review-ready product shell
tasks.description: Generate the SupplyExtract product, pricing, privacy, terms, refund and contact pages.
acceptance: All merchant-review pages render
Landing copy describes only implemented MVP functionality
No invented users, customers, accuracy or savings claims appear

tasks.title: PDF extraction API
tasks.description: Implement PDF validation, optional license validation and schema-constrained OpenAI extraction.
acceptance: Only application/pdf is accepted
Files over 10 MB are rejected
Uncertain values can remain null
Response includes editable header fields and line items

tasks.title: Review and export UI
tasks.description: Implement upload, editable review table and CSV/JSON download.
acceptance: User can edit all extracted fields
CSV includes one row per line item
JSON contains reviewed values
UI reminds users to verify extracted data

tasks.title: Lemon Squeezy entitlement
tasks.description: Validate paid license keys against the configured Lemon Squeezy subscription variant.
acceptance: Invalid license is rejected when paid mode is enabled
License metadata variant must match configured variant
No Lemon Squeezy secret is exposed to the browser

tasks.title: Privacy and retention verification
tasks.description: Verify app code does not persist uploaded PDF bytes and public privacy text accurately describes OpenAI processing.
acceptance: No application code writes uploaded PDF bytes to disk or database
Privacy page discloses third-party AI processing
No claim is made that upstream processors have zero retention

tasks.title: QA and launch preflight
tasks.description: Run lint/build plus merchant-review compliance checks.
acceptance: npm run lint passes
npm run build passes
Merchant-review source preflight passes
Core public routes and /api/health are ready for smoke testing

risks: AI extraction can be wrong; users must review output before relying on it
Supplier documents may contain confidential commercial information
Third-party AI processing must be disclosed accurately
A monthly document quota should not be marketed until persistent usage metering exists
Scanned or unusually complex PDFs may produce lower-quality extraction
Do not expand into bank statements or automated accounting approval without a separate risk/compliance review
